description: An AI tool that extracts and structures key terms from current policy documents and broker quotes (coverage limits, exclusions, deductibles, premium, renewal dates) into a standardized comparison table.

An AI assistant that retrieves and summarizes key coverage gaps, claim patterns, and risk exposures from the company's claims history and asset inventory, then flags which broker quotes address those gaps, assisting the human decision-maker.

A classifier that evaluates product condition photos against return policy eligibility criteria (damage, usage level, restocking requirements) and flags whether the return meets condition thresholds, with agent approval.

An AI assistant that retrieves order history and purchase date from the order management system and cross-references the return policy rules in real-time, surfacing eligibility status (in-window, out-of-window, needs exception) to the agent without requiring manual lookups across multiple systems.

An AI tool that automatically extracts transaction details (date, amount, description, reference codes) from bank statements and general ledger exports, standardizing formats and flagging data quality issues before manual matching begins.

A classifier that flags matched transaction pairs (bank statement line ↔ GL entry) as high-confidence, low-confidence, or unmatched, to triage which reconciling items need manual investigation versus which are routine and can be cleared quickly.

An AI tool that retrieves approved content from the calendar, matches it to platform-specific posting guidelines (LinkedIn, Instagram, Twitter/X, etc.), and generates a pre-filled scheduling form for each platform that the marketing user then verifies and publishes directly from the platform scheduler.

A classifier that reads approval sign-offs and content metadata and auto-categorizes posts as 'ready to schedule', 'pending approval', 'revisions needed', or 'approved but awaiting asset', enabling the marketing team to filter and prioritize their calendar view without manual status updates.

A classifier that reads incoming IT ticket descriptions and system logs, then assigns a severity level (critical, high, medium, low) and auto-populates the initial categorization based on the incident type and impact signals.

An AI assistant that searches incident history, system logs, and ticket database for similar issues when a new ticket arrives, surfacing likely duplicates or related tickets to the on-call engineer for rapid routing decision.

A classifier that takes sales transactions and applies the complex commission rule set (by region, product line, and exception flags) to automatically categorize each transaction into the correct commission tier and rate.

An AI tool that ingests employment contracts, ID documents, and tax forms from multiple submission channels, extracts key fields (name, role, start date, right-to-work status, tax details) and flags missing or incomplete documents.

A classifier that reviews the extracted and validated documents and automatically flags onboarding cases as 'ready-for-provisioning', 'needs-review', or 'documents-missing', determining which new hires can proceed to IT system access.

An AI tool that processes inspection photos and free-text notes to automatically extract and standardize hazard data into structured fields (hazard type, location, severity, root cause) aligned with the inspection checklist.

A classifier that flags corrective actions (from the logs) as on-track, overdue, or not-started based on the target close date and current status, surfacing untracked or stalled remediations without manual list checking.
